result.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines
result.comment: 108 pages total, 28 pages main text, 5 figures, 4 supplementary figures, 8 supplementary tables. Research article
result.summary: Maintaining up-to-date clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) is essential for evidence-based medicine, but rapid evidence growth and complex expert consensus formation limit timely updates. We developed GUIDE, a multi-agent copilot system for human-AI collaborative guideline generation and updating. GUIDE delegates labor-intensive tasks to specialized AI agents while preserving expert judgment and final arbitration. In 12 NICE ophthalmology datasets, GUIDE achieved 88.85% literature recall, 86.06% alignment in certainty-of-evidence ratings, and 91.67% recommendation agreement, requiring 162.17 minutes per dataset on average (28.68% human intervention). Performance remained stable across 20 additional datasets from cardiology, endocrinology, gastroenterology, and respiratory medicine. Ablation analysis showed that removing expert intervention reduced performance in judgment-intensive steps such as Risk-of-Bias assessment. In six post-cutoff datasets, GUIDE maintained robust end-to-end performance on unseen evidence. Prospective real-world validation showed that GUIDE reduced expert workload and produced more clinically acceptable recommendations than the original decade-old guideline (mean score, 3.73 vs. 1.53; agreement, 66.7% vs. 13.3%), with outcomes comparable to human-only updating (P = 0.588) but substantially less time and effort. GUIDE offers a practical framework for timely, trustworthy, expert-centric guideline development and validates computationally augmented consensus.

AI.brief_summary: GUIDE 是一个面向临床实践指南生成与更新的多智能体协作系统，把文献筛选、证据确定性分级、推荐形成等繁重步骤交给专用 AI agent，同时保留专家判断与最终仲裁，并在 NICE 眼科等 12 个数据集及多个学科数据上评估召回率、评分一致性与推荐一致性，还做了专家干预消融和前瞻验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联；但其多智能体证据聚合与专家仲裁机制、以及「判断密集步骤中去掉人类干预会掉分」的消融，可能为 latent 推理中的多假设筛选、证据可信度加权与停止/仲裁决策提供概念参照，可供核查。
